# Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map

## Original exercise

Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.

> 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
> with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
> \[
> \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
>       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
> \]

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
context.conclusion: For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n. The energy E:(0,∞)→ℝ is differentiable and E'(t)=0 for every t>0; consequently E is constant on (0,∞). The energy is exactly ∫_{ℝ^n}(|u_t|²+|Du|²) dx with no factor 1/2. No assertion at time zero is made.

record.type: Lebesgue measure and integral notation on real coordinate spaces
record.definition: For a natural dimension d, dx denotes standard Lebesgue measure on ℝ^d; integrals are Lebesgue integrals. In dimension zero the coordinate space is a singleton of measure one. On coordinate rectangles the measure is the product of the one-dimensional Lebesgue measures. For integrable real functions the integral has its usual real value.

record.type: Euclidean and differential notation for the smooth map u
record.definition: The dot denotes the Euclidean inner product on ℝ^m, |v| its Euclidean norm with |v|²=v·v. For x∈ℝ^n and t>0, u_t and u_tt are the first and second time derivatives of u; ∂_{x_j}u and ∂_{x_jx_j}u are its coordinate derivatives, for 1≤j≤n, taken component by component. Delta u=Δ_x u=Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u. The spatial gradient square |Du|² is the Frobenius square Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|². Mixed derivatives use the same componentwise convention.

binders.type: spatial coordinate index from 1 through n

record.definition: For every t>0, E(t)=∫_{ℝ^n}e(x,t) dx, with the Euclidean density e and Lebesgue measure dx specified above.

record.statement: For every x∈ℝ^n and t>0, u(x,t)·u_t(x,t)=0 and u_t(x,t)·(u_tt(x,t)−Delta u(x,t))=0. Moreover u·u_tt=−|u_t|² and u·∂_{x_jx_j}u=−|∂_{x_j}u|² for every 1≤j≤n; at each point every scalar a satisfying u_tt−Delta u=a u necessarily equals Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|², so u_tt−Delta u=(Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|²)u.

record.statement: For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n. More precisely, for every t0>0 there exist a compact C⊂ℝ^n and real R>0, η>0 and B≥0 with the following properties. Set J=[t0/2,3t0/2] and Q=[−R,R]^n. Then C⊂(−R,R)^n, |Q|=(2R)^n<∞, [t0−η,t0+η]⊂int J, and u(x,r)=q for x∉C,r∈J. All positive-order space/time derivatives of u vanish on (ℝ^n\C)×int J. The functions e and e_t are smooth. For every r∈int J and 1≤j≤n the spatial functions e(·,r), e_t(·,r), u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, u_t·∂_{x_j}u and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), evaluated at r, are continuous, supported in C, bounded on Q, measurable and absolutely integrable. For all x∈Q and r∈[t0−η,t0+η], |e_t(x,r)|≤B.
